chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah repels (calamity) through the one from our Shias who prays, from the one from our Shias who does not pray; and if they were all to agree upon neglecting the prayer, they would be destroyed.
And indeed, Allah repels through the one from our Shias who pays the alms-tax, from the one who does not pay; and if they were all to agree upon neglecting the alms-tax, they would be destroyed.
And indeed, Allah repels through the one from our Shias who performs the pilgrimage, from the one who does not; and if they were all to agree upon neglecting the pilgrimage, they would be destroyed.
And this is the Word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if it were not for Allah repelling some people by means of others, the earth would surely be corrupted.'
But Allah is Full of Bounty to the worlds.
So by Allah, it was not revealed except regarding you, and it did not mean by it anyone other than you.
ai.seo_question: How does the presence of righteous worshippers protect the entire Shia community from destruction according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'Daf'' (divine repulsion), where the righteous few preserve the community from general corruption, specifically linking the pillars of Salah, Zakat, and Hajj to collective survival. The Imam explicitly claims exclusive revelation of the cited verse (2:251) for the Shia, a point of scholarly debate regarding whether it refers to the broader Muslim community or the specific lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers.
